prompt.v: ABCD is a quadrilateral with all four corners on a circle, and ∠A = 105°. What is ∠C, in degrees?

problems.text: cyclic quadrilateral: angle A 105; find angle C
problems.explain: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°: each is half the arc it stands on, and the two arcs make the whole 360°. ∠C is opposite ∠A, so ∠C = 180 − 105 = 75°. (Not equal to it: that is a parallelogram’s rule.) So ∠C = 75°.

problems.explain: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°: each is half the arc it stands on, and the two arcs make the whole 360°. ∠B is opposite ∠D, so ∠B = 180 − 86 = 94°. (Not equal to it: that is a parallelogram’s rule.) So ∠B = 94°.

prompt.v: PA and PB are tangent to circle O at A and B, and ∠AOB = 100°. What is ∠APB, in degrees?

problems.text: two tangents: angle AOB 100; find angle APB
problems.explain: Each tangent meets its radius at 90°, so in quadrilateral OAPB two angles are 90° and the four add to 360°: ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180°. So it is 180 − 100 = 80°. (The two are supplementary, not equal.) So 80°.
